Weather (Heavy rain, wet asphalt) is a risk multiplier because it degrades traction and visibility. Dispatch status (Running 20 minutes behind schedule) is a genuine risk factor because the driver is under pressure to make up time. All three fields are genuine risk multipliers.

Cargo is dry goods/general freight, which is not a risk factor. Weather is clear/dry, which is not a risk factor. Dispatch status is on schedule, which is not a risk factor. Since none of the fields are risk multipliers and the dispatch status indicates a controlled condition, the severity should be lowered.
